exposure: Microbial wound contamination (Escherichia coli and Enterococcus spp.)
outcome: Suppuration in the anterior abdominal wall
cohort: The study included 313 female patients who underwent cesarean section, categorized into a control group and three groups based on their degree of obesity.
finding: Long-term intraabdominal hypertension during the postoperative period is a significant risk factor for postoperative infectious complications in obese maternity patients following cesarean section, and SSI incidence increased with higher degrees of obesity.
